PAT margin expanded 595 bps YoY to 8.8% Internal Accruals to Fund Mix Upgrade and Margin Expansion Having largely completed its deleveraging, with Net Debt/EBITDA down to 3.1x (2.2x adjusted) and the effective interest rate at 7.8%, SAMHI has turned into a self-funding platform, generating ~INR 830 Mn of free cash flow in Q2FY27 alone. That cash is now being redeployed into a secured pipeline of ~1,670 rooms (addition of 672 keys by FY29E), anchored by W-Hyderabad (170 keys), with a possible ~INR 1.7 Bn of revenue at stabilisation, lifting upscale income share towards ~60% by FY30E. Alongside, RARE India adds a capex-light fee stream from FY28E. We believe this combination of same-store compounding, new openings and a margin-accretive mix is forecast to drive a revenue/Adj. PAT CAGR of ~15.5%/66.2% over FY26–FY29E. Sold-out Nights at 37% Underpin Pricing Power SAMHI’s Q2FY27 RevPAR rose 14.3% YoY to INR 5,746, driven by ARR growth of 9.2% and occupancy expansion to 78.6% (vs. 75.0%). Sold-out nights rose to 37% in this quarter (vs. 32%) and demand remained domestic-led (~80% of room nights). Net office absorption of ~7.9 Mn sq. ft across Bengaluru and Hyderabad offset a ~4% YoY decline in air traffic from route rationalisation. ARR growth is expected to sustain, supported by a richer Upper Upscale mix from rebranding and new openings. View and Valuation We revise our FY27E / FY28E EBITDA estimate upwards by 5.4% / 2.5%, factoring in the Q2FY27 beat and rate-led RevPAR growth of 14.3% YoY. SAMHI's corporate-led occupancy engine (78.6%) and the capex-light ‘RARE India’ platform, live from Q3FY27E, are anticipated to drive earnings expansion. Additionally, a self-funded balance sheet (Net Debt/EBITDA at 3.1x) reinforces our conviction. We retain our target price of INR 240, based on a target EV/EBITDA multiple of 11.0x (~17% discount to peer median) on FY28E Adj. EBITDA, confirming it through DCF valuation. Given an upside of ~50%, we retain our 'BUY' rating on the stock.
